Thanks for carving out time today — good conversation. Below is a concise readout from our deep‑dive and a mutual action plan (MAP) so we can keep momentum. If any item is inaccurate, please flag edits inline.

High‑level summary
- Primary use case: real‑time document enrichment (multi‑turn assistant + retrieval) for support workflows.
- Primary pain: tail latency spikes at peak business hours (customer SLA p95 target currently ~300ms; internal goal 120ms).
- Expected steady RPS: 350 requests/sec (avg) with 800 RPS peak (burst windows 10–15m). Average prompt length ~350 tokens, model output avg ~120 tokens.

Key technical constraints we discussed
- Latency target: p95 <= 120ms for 1k tokens end‑to‑end (model inference only budget ~80–100ms).
- Throughput: sustained 350 RPS, burst capacity to 800 RPS.
- Model requirements: high‑quality open LLM acceptable; preference toward 13B‑to‑34B class quantized models for cost/latency tradeoff. We noted potential evaluation on a 13B quantized variant + a 34B fallback.
- KV/prefix cache: heavy reuse on session prompts — prefix caching will materially reduce per‑token work if managed at routing layer.
- Multi‑tenant vs dedicated: you indicated regulated data for a subset of customers — Dedicated pools (or Private VPC) recommended for those tenants.

Suggested topology (brief)
- Edge ingress -> regional routing -> short‑seq optimized model pool (13B q4) for low latency -> fallback pool (34B quantized) for higher quality when budget permits.
- Smart routing rules: latency SLO first, cost threshold second; automated fallback to cached responses for repeated prompts.

Immediate asks / Mutual Action Plan (owners & ETA)
1) TransitAI to provide 2 weeks of tokenized traffic sample (anonymized) for us to run our batch latency & batching simulation. Owner: Liam. ETA: 2028‑06‑16.
2) Redwood to deliver a preliminary capacity estimate and cost model (includes burst runways + warm‑start sizing). Owner: Naomi/Sean. ETA: 2028‑06‑12 (attached: transitai-load‑estimates.xlsx).
3) Engineering deep‑dive: 60–90m workshop focusing on KV cache patterns and routing rules. Proposed time: week of 2028‑06‑19. Owner: Karthik/TransitAI Eng.
4) Procurement intro & docs: TransitAI to share procurement timeline and SOC2/attestation needs. Owner: Priya. ETA: 2028‑06‑14.

Attachments referenced: transitai-load‑estimates.xlsx (initial cost/capacity sketch). I also attached a topology sketch in the follow up email.

Next immediate step: Liam — please drop the anonymized traffic export to the drive link above or send to naomi@redwood.com. We'll run the batch simulation and return a latency profile and recommended pool sizes.

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop.

Liam — quick answers inline: 

1) Tokenization: we use GPT‑2 style BPE by default in our benchmarking pipeline. For code blocks we'll run a separate tokenization pass; long literals can increase token count by ~15–30%. If you can strip PII and long logs that will keep the sample representative.

2) Burst policy recommendation: hybrid. Reserve a small committed pool to cover base & predictable windows (we size that to 60–70% of observed peak) and configure burst (ephemeral) pools for unexpected spikes. This minimizes committed spend while keeping SLOs. We'll show cost + latency tradeoffs in the capacity estimate.

3) Cancellation / billing: Redwood supports request cancellation. We bill only for completed tokens; partial outputs are not charged if the request was programmatically cancelled within the runtime window. We'll document edge cases in the runbook.

Attached: redwood‑topology‑sketch.pdf — a quick sketch of the proposed routing and cache placement.
